subject.title: BL-ecommerce-engagement-01: notify requests with unknown EANs are retried forever and never cleaned up

question: Should deleted-or-missing product notify rows be terminally closed by the cron, or should only new invalid signups be rejected while existing rows remain pending for possible catalog return?
rationale: Two open PRs encode different retention policies for products that disappear after signup, and automation should not choose that business rule without owner intent.

options.title: Close orphan rows in the cron
options.body: Merge the broader fix path from https://github.com/Hamelyn-SL/hamelyn-serverless/pull/7198 so missing-product rows stop retrying and new invalid signups are rejected.

options.title: Reject only new unknown products
options.body: Use the narrower signup-only path from https://github.com/Hamelyn-SL/hamelyn-serverless/pull/7143 if pending rows for removed products must be preserved for later catalog return.

recommendation.title: Close orphan rows in the cron
recommendation.body: Merge the broader fix path from https://github.com/Hamelyn-SL/hamelyn-serverless/pull/7198 so missing-product rows stop retrying and new invalid signups are rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the reporter and authored the BL extraction/fix context that frames the retention-policy choice.
